# Local-First Software

## Overview
The "Local-First [IoT](./iot.md)" lunch-and-learn session held on July 5 featured invited guest presenter Alex Kim from [TeaBuddy](./teabuddy.md) at the [Aurora Labs](./aurora-labs.md) office. The session explored the practical application of local-first software and [hardware](./hardware.md) principles in consumer electronics, specifically examining why certain consumer gadgets reject cloud infrastructure in favor of local control and direct connectivity.

## Key Details
* **Presenter:** Alex Kim (TeaBuddy, invited guest at the Aurora office)
* **Core Topics Discussed:**
  * [Bluetooth Low Energy](./bluetooth-low-energy.md) ([BLE](./ble.md)) versus mesh network tradeoffs for consumer gadgets.
  * The rationale behind TeaBuddy's decision to reject cloud accounts for version 1 of their product.
  * A live demonstration comparing a puck buzzer and [Nova Widget](./nova-widget.md) LED patterns.
* **Q&A Highlights:**
  * [Mira](./aurora-nova-widget-v2.md) noted that mesh network complexity becomes worthwhile when scaling to six or more garden [sensors](./sensors.md).
  * Alex Kim emphasized that tea drinkers prefer devices designed for "one device, one job" simplicity.
  * Jonah offered to share enclosure supplier contacts.
* **Action Items:** Add a cross-link wiki page to `teabuddy-cross-ref` (noting it may already exist).

* **Alex Kim:** Guest presenter representing TeaBuddy.

* **Jonah:** Participant in the Q&A who offered supplier contact information.

* **Local-First IoT:** Designing Internet of Things devices that operate independently of cloud servers and user accounts.
* **BLE vs Mesh Tradeoffs:** Evaluating the range, [power consumption](./power-consumption.md), and network topology decisions for low-power wireless consumer hardware.
